title: Senior Project: DIY Suspension Dyno
summary: Scotch Yoke-based suspension dyno for testing bike shocks.
content: I designed, prototyped, and manufactured my own suspension dynamometer from scratch to analyze mountain bike rear shocks' compression and rebound characteristics. The test rig uses an S-type load cell to measure force and a magnetic rotary encoder to measure displacement, synchronized via serial output on an Arduino. A Scotch yoke drive system ensures smooth cyclic motion. Python is used to parse the incoming serial data in real time, generating live force vs. velocity and force vs. displacement plots. The system allows tuners and riders to visualize damping curves and optimize setup. All components were prototyped, manually machined, and integrated over several months as a senior capstone project. Future plans include motorized automation, battery integration, and open-sourcing the final design for DIY enthusiasts.

title: Anodizing Station
summary: Custom aluminum anodizing setup for bike parts and engineering art.
content: This project was completed as part of my 10th grade Chemistry class, where I decided to create a nine inch square puzzle from 6061 aluminum. The pieces were waterjet-cut and then anodized to explore surface coating and material transformation. Each piece was measured using micrometers to assess the thickness increase from anodizing. The process taught me how to handle hazardous chemicals safely and showed how much you can accomplish using everyday resources from the hardware store.

title: Potato Cannon
summary: A fun AP Physics project demonstrating projectile motion.
content: I helped construct and perform data analysis for an AP Physics group final project. We explored classic kinematics and projectile motion, and ended up with a powerful air-powered potato cannon. I learned how to do: video analysis, PVC construction, water sprinkler valve 'hacking', and group collaboration skills. Build reference inspired by M. Beckler’s pneumatic cannon guide.

title: PLTW: Compound Ballistics
summary: Engineering class project - game design and simple mechanics.
content: This was a PLTW High school project in which we addressed the challenge of creating a large-scale yard game similar to the classic board game Battleship. We were tasked with building a ping pong launching machine that would compete against other machines. The catch was that they had to be powered with 2 rubber bands. We ultimately didn't have the most successful design, but I helped guide the mechanics of the launcher and did the mechanical advantage research.

title: PLTW: Historical Design Chess Pieces
summary: Historical design research and modeling in Fusion 360.
content: PLTW historical design challenge, modeled and 3D printed chess pieces based on the works of Richard Dick Teague (AMC Pacer)

title: Smart Home Analog HVAC Control
summary: Design Challenge from Sonoma Clean Power, ESP32 Project
content: I was a part of a design team in my PLTW class that addressed the Duck Curve Challenge by Sonoma Clean Power. I was the design lead and did the full system integration. What is the Duck Curve? Every year, Sonoma Clean Power challenges high school students to develop a behavioral or physical solution to address the grid stress during peak energy use hours. Our solution mitigated HVAC usage while windows were left open. Using an ESP32, reed switches, and relays, we cut the cooling wire on older HVAC systems when a window was open. We built a testing board and prototyped an AC-to-DC logic module. The project was designed for use in classrooms, dorms, and other retrofitted buildings.

title: PLTW: Balsa Wood Bridge
summary: Exploration of statics and civil engineering principles.
content: This was a civil engineering unit from my Principles of Engineering PLTW class. We were challenged to construct a balsa wood bridge using wood glue and paper gussets. We explored statics, bridge simulation software, and design considerations when building infrastructure. My bridge withstood __N and had a strength to weight ratio of __.

title: PLTW: AI Robotics Design Challenge
summary: AI image recognition powered pet feeder
content: At the end of my first year of PLTW, I was a co-lead (mechanical) on a robotics final. We were tasked with creating a household product that used AI image recognition to drive a VEX robotics project. We designed a pet feeder that uses Google's programmable image recognition to identify a pet and open its assigned bowl. The project featured a garage door-like mechanical system with individual motors per bowl. We showcased our work at a mock investor expo in our STEM core.
